chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: The Kentucky Club, Victor sessions and arranging
summary: Howard says Charlie Lawrence did the arranging for the Victor sessions, and Lloyd Reese wrote a little.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, because that's good to know, that he was an outstanding saxophone and clarinetist too. I didn't know that. Let's see, it said something about Paul's band was playing at the Kentucky Club on Central Avenue. Do you remember anything about the Kentucky Club?
Yeah. The Kentucky Club was just a little club with (inaudible) Leon Herrford (inaudible).
What about Lewis Taylor? Lewis Taylor?
Lewis Taylor?
What did Lewis play?
Trombone.
Uh-huh.
But he came later, afterwards.
I see.
He didn't begin with us, because he left another band and came over to the Quality.
Uh-huh. Okay. Then what about some of those Victor recording sessions? Do you remember anything about those? Did you do any writing for those?
No, I didn't do any writing.
Who did the writing, anybody you knew of?
Charlie.
Charlie Lawrence.
Charlie Lawrence.
He was the arranger, huh?
Yeah, he was an arranger, and a good one.
I've heard so much about him, you know.
Yeah.
Lloyd Reese used to rave about him you know.
Huh?
Lloyd Reese used to rave about him a lot.
Huh?
Lloyd Reese used to talk about Charlie Lawrence a lot.
Oh, yeah, Lloyd. Lloyd played in the band. He played with that band.
Uh-huh. Was Lloyd ever doing any writing that you know of?
Yes, he did a little. Not too much.
Not like Charles, huh?
He did some. You would know he was there anyhow.
Uh-huh.
When he'd go out to do something, Lloyd would sit down and start to tearing up the music, you know.
Uh-huh. He was always one that wanted to do things quite well, you know.
Oh, yeah, wanted to do things quite well.
Uh-huh.
You're right. Very, very, very good at his presentations.
Uh-huh.
Yeah.
Now, Lloyd was first a saxophone player and then later added trumpet.
Well, let me see. I can't think of who else we had, added.
No, in other words, I mean since Lloyd Reese played saxophone and trumpet was he a saxophone player first?
Yes.
